page.overview:
What is Ruyi Jingu Bang?

The staff is initially described as a pillar of black iron, twenty feet in height and the width of a barrel. After shrinking to the size Wukong mainly uses when wielding, it is only a little taller than him, and as thick as a rice bowl. The weapon is banded with a gold ring at each of its ends. An inscription runs along its body, denoting its name as the "Compliant Golden-Hooped Staff" and its weight as "thirteen thousand five hundred catties", which is approximately 7,960 kg (17,550 lbs). Due to its huge size and monstrously heavy weight, few beings besides Wukong are able to even lift the staff.

The inscription indicates that the staff follows the commands of its owner, shrinking or growing to his whim, and make copies of itself.

The Ruyi Jingu Bang was originally one of the massive nails that Yu the Great used to set the depth of rivers and seas in order to prevent flooding. It was placed in the treasury of the Dragon Palace of the East Sea.

When Sun Wukong went to the palace to find a weapon he could use, the Ruyi Jingu Bang began glowing auspiciously. The Dragon Queen noticed this and suggested to her husband Ao Guang to give the rod to Sun Wukong after every other weapon in their armoury proved too light for him.
